cases.description: No rules: runRules returns the transaction unchanged apart from derived fields.
A rule whose condition matches nothing leaves the transaction unchanged.
A payee-is rule matches the resolved payee ID; a display name or an unresolved payee does not.
An imported_payee rule matches the raw bank text case-insensitively and renames the payee.
imported_payee is "" matches empty and null text; an absent imported_payee is treated as empty by string conditions.
imported_payee oneOf is found through the first-character rule index.
Rules that set notes to null and to an empty string, in separate stages.
prepend-notes and append-notes on null, empty and populated notes.
A rule sets a transfer payee; the category and account stay as they are.
A later payee-is rule sees the payee an earlier rule set, but payee_name is computed once before any rule runs.
A lone payee-isNot rule runs for every payee but the excluded one.
A rule with both a payee and an imported_payee condition is indexed under both values, so a candidate lookup can skip it even when an or join would match.
Id-typed conditions on an absent field never match, while null matches is-null.
A rule on an off-budget account sets a category.
matches with escaped metacharacters; the pattern is lowercased and the text is lowercased.
The value is lowercased before it is compiled, so \D in a pattern behaves as \d.
isapprox uses a 7.5% rounded threshold: -10000 spans -10750..-9250; a small value has threshold 0.
isbetween sorts its bounds and is inclusive; inflow and outflow options flip the sign handling.
A zero amount against inflow and outflow options.
date conditions with a recurrence object: exact, approximate, weekend skip and an ended series.
date is with a month value and a year value.
A transaction without a schedule that matches a schedule rule gets the schedule linked; a completed schedule rule is still a rule upstream.
A transaction already attached to a schedule runs that schedule rule without its conditions and skips other schedules rules.
Schedule rules with an exact date and a payee: the active one links its schedule; upstream also links a completed schedule.
A user rule links a schedule; the schedule is set on the output.
Two rules set the same category in one stage; the higher-scored (is) rule runs later and wins over contains.
Pre, default and post rules set the same category; post wins. Ids are the reverse of stage order.
Two equally scored rules in one stage run in id order; the later id wins.
A rule of only exact operators is scored double and runs after looser rules in the same stage.
contains, matches and hasTags with accents, ligature-like capitals, a dotted capital I and emoji.
hasTags requires a whole tag: not a prefix, not a double hash, not mid-word.
delete-transaction sets the tombstone; later rules still run.
BALANCE_OF by account id, by name, for an unknown account, and on the same day as history.
